message.content:
Here are some practical tips to keep your piano in top shape:

| Category | Tip | Why It Helps |
|----------|-----|--------------|
| **Daily Care** | Keep the piano in a stable environment (no direct sunlight, no drafts, and moderate humidity). | Fluctuating temperature/humidity can warp the soundboard and cause cracks. |
| | Dust the keys and lid with a soft, dry cloth after each use. | Prevents dust buildup that can affect key action and appearance. |
| | Avoid placing heavy objects on the piano. | Excess weight can stress the frame and soundboard. |
| **Key Maintenance** | Check for loose or sticking keys weekly. | Early detection prevents more serious action problems. |
| | Use a key cleaner or a mild soap solution (water + a drop of dish soap) to clean the keys. | Keeps the keys free of grime without damaging the finish. |
| **Pedal Care** | Inspect the pedals for wear and ensure they return smoothly. | Pedal issues can affect sustain and overall playability. |
| | Lubricate the pedal mechanisms with a light machine oil (if needed). | Reduces friction and prolongs pedal life. |
| **Soundboard & Strings** | Keep the piano away from direct heat sources (radiators, heaters). | Heat can dry out the wood and cause cracks. |
| | If you notice a noticeable change in tone or a “dead” note, schedule a tuning. | Tuning keeps the strings at proper tension and restores tonal balance. |
| **Professional Care** | Have a qualified technician tune the piano at least twice a year (or more if you play often). | Professional tuning ensures accurate pitch and balanced tone. |
| | Schedule a full inspection (action, hammers, strings, soundboard) every 3–5 years. | Detects hidden issues before they become costly repairs. |
| **Cleaning** | Use a piano-specific cleaning solution for the lid and outer surfaces. | Protects the finish and prevents damage from harsh chemicals. |
| | Clean the inside of the lid (if accessible) with a soft brush to remove dust. | Maintains resonance and prevents dust from affecting sound. |
| **Storage** | If you need to store the piano, keep it in a climate-controlled room. | Prevents warping and cracking during storage. |
| | Use a piano cover to protect from dust and light. | Keeps the piano looking fresh and reduces cleaning frequency. |
| **General Tips** | Avoid playing the piano in extremely humid or dry conditions. | Extreme humidity can cause the wood to expand/contract, leading to cracks. |
| | Keep pets away from the piano. | Pets can scratch or damage the keys and lid. |
| | Use a piano stand or a padded base if you need to move it. | Protects the frame and soundboard from impact. |

### Quick Checklist (for a quick glance)

- [ ] Stable temperature & humidity
- [ ] Dust keys & lid daily
- [ ] Inspect pedals weekly
- [ ] Tune twice a year
- [ ] Full inspection every 3–5 years
- [ ] Clean with piano-specific products
- [ ] Store in climate-controlled space if needed

By following these steps, you’ll preserve the piano’s sound quality, extend its lifespan, and reduce the likelihood of costly repairs. Happy playing!
